statements.text: Across model specifications, adding TLS scores raised the bootstrapped area under the ROC curve by between 0.02 and 0.09.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: bootstrapped changes in area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve ranged from 0.0002 to 0.0089
statements.note: The reported gains were ten times smaller, 0.0002 to 0.0089, which the abstract characterises as no meaningful incremental value.

statements.text: In TCGA-BRCA, strict-consensus TLS status showed no association with nodal positivity, with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.95 and a confidence interval spanning 1.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Strict-consensus TLS status was not associated with nodal positivity in TCGA-BRCA (adjusted odds ratio: 0.95, 95% confidence interval: 0.62-1.45, P = 0.822).
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly this null result with OR 0.95 and CI 0.62-1.45.

statements.text: TLS signature scores were higher in tumours with abundant tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes on histological review.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Three published TLS signatures were scored by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis in oestrogen receptor-positive luminal tumours.
statements.note: TLS status was derived purely from transcriptomic signatures; no histological lymphocyte assessment or comparison is reported.

statements.text: The study concludes that a TLS signature should not replace sentinel lymph node biopsy in oestrogen receptor-positive luminal breast cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: These data do not support replacing sentinel lymph node biopsy with a TLS signature in oestrogen receptor-positive luminal breast cancer.
statements.note: This is the abstract's closing conclusion, stated almost in these terms.

statements.text: HERV upregulation in gastric tumours results from loss of DNA methylation at the HERV loci.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Differential and functional analysis indicated that these HERV elements significantly impacted the cell cycle, with their upregulation linked to tumor growth both in vitro and in vivo.
statements.note: The abstract describes downstream consequences of HERV upregulation but never proposes or tests a cause such as DNA methylation.

statements.text: Tumour tissue contained 113 upregulated and 46 downregulated endogenous transposable elements relative to adjacent non-tumour tissue.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Analysis of dysregulated ETEs revealed 113 upregulated and 46 downregulated ETEs in tumor tissues compared to adjacent non-tumor tissues.
statements.note: The counts and direction match the abstract exactly.

statements.text: The four HERV elements performed worse than conventional biomarkers in diagnosing gastric cancer.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The diagnostic performance of the four HERV elements surpassed that of conventional biomarkers and improved with combined biomarker analysis.
statements.note: The abstract states the HERV elements surpassed conventional biomarkers, the opposite direction.

statements.text: Patients in the HERVs-high group had larger tumours, higher grade and more lymph node metastasis than the HERVs-low group.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Higher HERVs expression (HERVs high ) correlated with larger tumor size, higher grade, increased lymph node metastasis, and higher Odds ratio compared to lower expression (HERVs low ) groups.
statements.note: All three clinical correlates are listed for the HERVs-high group in the abstract.

statements.text: MLL2 maintains H3K4me3 and H3K27ac at young LINE-1 elements and prevents repressive H3K9me3 from accumulating there.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: is critical for maintaining their active state (H3K4me3 and H3K27ac), while preventing the accumulation of repressive H3K9me3
statements.note: The abstract reports both the active marks maintained and the repressive mark kept away at L1 5'UTRs.

statements.text: The MLL2-bound L1 elements are enriched near genes that drive neural differentiation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: modulating the expression of neighboring genes in ESC and, more prominently, during differentiation
statements.note: Neighbouring genes are mentioned, but no gene category or lineage is named and differentiation is unspecified.

statements.text: The study confirms that MLL2's main function is to counteract Polycomb repression at bivalent promoters of developmental genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: primary role is not to oppose Polycomb-mediated repression at the bivalent promoters of developmental genes
statements.note: The abstract explicitly rejects this prevailing view.

statements.text: Targeted deletions showed that MLL2-bound L1 elements act as enhancers, with stronger effects during differentiation than in ESC.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we demonstrate that these MLL2-bound L1 elements act as enhancers, modulating the expression of neighboring genes in ESC and, more prominently, during differentiation
statements.note: Enhancer function and the more prominent effect during differentiation are both stated.

statements.text: Among NSCLC patients progressing on first- or second-generation TKIs, EGFR T790M was detected in 48.4%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: EGFR T790M was detected in 48.4% of patients who progressed on 1st/2nd-generation TKIs.
statements.note: The percentage and population match the abstract.

statements.text: The study enrolled 48 patients, 42 with HR+/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and 6 with EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: 48 metastatic patients (42 with EGFR-mutant NSCLC; 6 with HR+/HER2-negative MBC)
statements.note: The cohort sizes are swapped: 42 had NSCLC and only 6 had breast cancer.

statements.text: In the breast cancer cohort, changes in ctDNA fractional abundance anticipated progression by up to nine months before imaging confirmed it.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Variations in ctDNA fractional abundance predicted disease progression up to 9 months before radiological confirmation.
statements.note: The lead time of up to 9 months is reported for the MBC cohort.

statements.text: Patients whose T790M was detected in ctDNA were switched to a third-generation TKI and had longer progression-free survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study provides real-world evidence that ddPCR-based ctDNA monitoring enables early detection of resistance and predicts disease progression significantly earlier than standard imaging in both NSCLC and MBC.
statements.note: The abstract reports detection and lead time but no treatment changes or outcomes following detection.

statements.text: Tumours with RNA-detected chromosome 3 loss had shorter metastasis-free survival than tumours without it.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Uveal melanoma is a lethal intraocular tumour, in which the presence of certain genetic alterations correlates with the risk of metastatic dissemination and patient survival.
statements.note: The prognostic link is background; the study measures detectability of alterations from RNA, not patient outcomes.

statements.text: RNA analysis of the TCGA cohort uncovered three BAP1 and five EIF1AX mutations that the original DNA sequencing had missed.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: in the TCGA cohort we detected previously unreported mutations in BAP1 (n=3) and EIF1AX (n=5), that were missed by the original DNA sequencing.
statements.note: The counts for both genes are given explicitly.

statements.text: In the five prospective cases, every mutation and copy number alteration was recovered from RNA by combining the described approaches.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In our prospective cohort, all mutations and copy number alterations were successfully identified at the RNA level by combining the described approaches.
statements.note: The abstract reports complete detection in the prospective cohort.

statements.text: Unsupervised gene expression profiling reliably identified all clinically relevant genetic alterations, including chromosome 3 status.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Unsupervised gene expression profiling strongly correlated to the presence of chromosome 3 alterations, but was not reliable in identifying other (clinically-)relevant genetic alterations.
statements.note: Expression profiling tracked chromosome 3 only and was explicitly unreliable for the other alterations.

statements.text: Comparing low-grade tumour patients with controls yielded 85 differentially expressed platelet genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: and 85 genes in high-grade tumor patients vs. low-grade tumor patients. No genes met significance in low-grade tumor patients vs. controls.
statements.note: The 85 genes were for high-grade versus low-grade; low-grade versus controls produced no significant genes.

statements.text: Platelet transcriptomic signatures returned to normal after surgical resection of the tumour.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings support the feasibility of tumor-educated platelets as a minimally invasive biomarker for pediatric malignant brain tumor detection, and longitudinal monitoring.
statements.note: Longitudinal monitoring is proposed as a future use; no post-treatment samples or changes are reported.

statements.text: A logistic regression classifier of platelet transcripts identified high-grade tumour patients with AUC 0.89, 79% sensitivity and 80% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: achieved an area under the curve of 0.89, sensitivity of 79%, and a specificity of 80% in identifying high-grade tumor patients.
statements.note: All three performance figures match the abstract.

statements.text: Platelets from high-grade tumour patients consistently overexpressed mitochondrial genes associated with cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: High-grade tumor patients showed consistent upregulation of cancer-associated mitochondrial genes.
statements.note: The abstract reports this upregulation specifically in high-grade patients.

statements.text: Of 46 patients, nine (19.6%) recurred, and five of those recurrences involved extra-abdominal disease.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Nine patients recurred (19.6%), most with extra-abdominal disease (n = 5, or 55.6%).
statements.note: Both the recurrence count and the extra-abdominal subset are stated.

statements.text: Patients with abnormal p53 had a higher recurrence rate than the MMR-deficient patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: 6 had abnormal p53 (13.0%), and 12 were p53 wildtype (26.1%). There were no recurrences in the POLE subgroup.
statements.note: Recurrence is broken down only for the POLE group and by mutational signature, not for p53 or MMR groups.

statements.text: The most common dominant mutational signature was SBS15 or SBS44, found in 17 of the 38 patients with a dominant signature.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: 17 SBS5 signature (44.7%), 10 SBS15 or SBS44 signature (26.3%)
statements.note: SBS5 was the most common at 17 patients; SBS15/SBS44 accounted for 10.

statements.text: No patient in the POLE-mutated subgroup experienced a recurrence.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: There were no recurrences in the POLE subgroup.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: The kochia genome assembly totals 969.6 Mb with a scaffold N50 of 99.88 Mb.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a total length of 969.6 Mb, and an N50 scaffold length of 99.88 Mb
statements.note: Both assembly metrics are given in the background section.

statements.text: Genes carrying FHY3 or FAR1 domains have contracted in kochia relative to related species.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: genes containing Far-Red Elongated Hypocotyl 3 (FHY3) or Far-Red Impaired Response 1 (FAR1) functional domains have undergone a large, kochia-specific gene family expansion.
statements.note: The abstract reports a large kochia-specific expansion, not a contraction.

statements.text: Muntjac elements are transcriptionally active in glyphosate-resistant kochia populations growing in the field.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we characterized a new MuDR subtype, named here as 'Muntjac', which contributes to the evolution of herbicide resistance in kochia through the process of transduplication.
statements.note: Muntjac is characterised from genome structure; expression and field populations are not mentioned.

statements.text: MuDR-like transposons carrying FHY3/FAR1 domains were closely linked to duplicated copies of the EPSPS gene that confer glyphosate resistance.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: putative Mutator Don-Robertson (MuDR) transposable elements with detectable FHY3/FAR1 domains were tightly associated with segmental duplications of 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase subsequently conferring resistance to the herbicide glyphosate.
statements.note: EPSPS is 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase; the tight association with its duplications is stated.

statements.text: Patients with KRAS p.G12D detectable in preoperative cfDNA had shorter survival after resection.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Somatic mutation detection from liquid biopsy using dPCR further supports its potential utility in the preoperative setting.
statements.note: The abstract reports detection rates only; no survival or outcome data are given.

statements.text: In tumour tissue, the two platforms agreed on 58.3% of KRAS p.G12D calls and 71.4% of TP53 p.R273H calls.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The concordance between both platforms was 71.4% for KRAS p.G12D and 58.3% for the analysis of TP53 p.R273H mutations in tumor tissue.
statements.note: The two concordance figures are swapped: 71.4% for KRAS and 58.3% for TP53.

statements.text: In plasma cfDNA, dPCR found KRAS p.G12D in 10.2% and TP53 p.R273H in 2.0% of samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In cfDNA, dPCR identified KRAS p.G12D in 10.2% and TP53 p.R273H in 2.0% of samples.
statements.note: The cfDNA detection rates match exactly.

statements.text: Low DNA yield restricted mutation detection in extracellular vesicle-associated DNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Mutation detection in EV-DNA was limited by low DNA yield.
statements.note: Stated directly for EV-DNA.

statements.text: C4orf50 expression correlated more strongly with the ESTIMATE Stromal Score than with the Immune Score.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: correlated positively with the ESTIMATE Immune Score (rho =0.372), Stromal Score (rho =0.198)
statements.note: The Immune Score correlation (rho 0.372) was almost double the Stromal Score correlation (rho 0.198).

statements.text: Comparing 1,093 breast tumours with 111 normal tissues, C4orf50 was expressed at higher levels in the tumours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: C4orf50 expression was higher in 1,093 breast tumor samples than in 111 normal samples
statements.note: The sample counts and direction are stated in the results.

statements.text: Each standard-deviation increase in C4orf50 expression was linked to a 41% higher hazard of death in the stratified Cox model.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: higher continuous C4orf50 expression was associated with poorer overall survival [hazard ratio (HR) per 1 standard deviation =1.41, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.19-1.67
statements.note: HR 1.41 per SD corresponds to a 41% higher hazard.

statements.text: Knockdown of C4orf50 in breast cancer cell lines reduces proliferation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These observational findings do not establish a causal role for C4orf50 and require validation in independent cohorts and experimental models.
statements.note: No experiments were performed; the abstract explicitly leaves functional effects open.

statements.text: The study drew on RNA-seq data from 648 TCGA glioma samples and 325 CGGA samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data of 648 glioma samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and 325 samples from the Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA)
statements.note: Both cohort sizes are stated in the methods.

statements.text: High NR2F6 expression was associated with a favourable prognosis in glioma patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: a significant upregulation of NR2F6 expression in high-grade gliomas, which is associated with an unfavorable prognosis in patients.
statements.note: The abstract links NR2F6 upregulation to an unfavourable, not favourable, prognosis.

statements.text: NR2F6 expression is higher in MGMT-unmethylated than in MGMT-methylated glioblastomas.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We observed a significant upregulation of NR2F6 expression in high-grade gliomas
statements.note: MGMT promoter methylation status is never mentioned.

statements.text: NR2F6 was significantly upregulated in TMZ-resistant glioma cells and conferred resistance through the E2F2-PARP1 axis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: our findings revealed a significant upregulation of NR2F6 in drug-resistant cells, which induced TMZ resistance in glioma cells via the E2F2-PARP1 axis.
statements.note: Both the upregulation in resistant cells and the E2F2-PARP1 mechanism are stated.

statements.text: The novel consensus clustering method split liver cancer patients into exactly two subtypes, named CS1 and CS2.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we developed a novel consensus clustering method that categorizes liver cancer patients into two subtypes, CS1 and CS2.
statements.note: Two subtypes, CS1 and CS2, are stated in the results.

statements.text: Patients in the CS2 subtype had worse overall survival than those in CS1.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we investigated the mechanisms driving prognostic variations among distinct subtypes.
statements.note: Prognostic variation between subtypes is mentioned, but which subtype fares worse is never stated.

statements.text: The prognostic model outperformed several models published in the preceding five years.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: which demonstrated superior predictive accuracy compared to several models published in the past five years.
statements.note: The abstract claims superior accuracy against recent published models.

statements.text: CS1 and CS2 did not differ in fatty acid metabolism or hypoxia levels.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we observed differences between CS1 and CS2 in various metabolic pathways, biological processes, and signaling pathways, such as fatty acid metabolism, hypoxia levels, PI3K-AKT and MIF signaling pathway.
statements.note: Fatty acid metabolism and hypoxia are named as differences between the subtypes.

statements.text: Patients with lower DELFI-TF scores during treatment had a median overall survival of 29.1 months versus 62.8 months for higher scores.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients with lower DELFI-TF scores during treatment have longer overall survival (62.8 vs 29.1 months
statements.note: The direction is reversed: lower scores went with the longer survival of 62.8 months.

statements.text: DELFI-TF scores correlated with ctDNA levels with a Pearson r of 0.90.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: DELFI-TF scores strongly correlate with circulating tumor DNA levels (ctDNA) (r = 0.90, p < 0.0001, Pearson correlation)
statements.note: The correlation coefficient is given as r = 0.90.

statements.text: DELFI-TF scores fell in patients who responded to immunotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: DELFI-TF scores prior to therapy initiation are associated with clinical response
statements.note: The abstract names no therapy type and describes no score trajectories by response.

statements.text: The method was validated in two independent cohorts, one of colorectal and one of lung cancer patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: validate the method in two independent cohorts of patients with colorectal or lung cancer.
statements.note: Two independent cohorts with these cancer types are stated.

statements.text: The siRNA screen covered all 204 known and putative human nucleases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: small interfering RNA screen that targeted all 204 known and putative human nucleases
statements.note: The screen size of 204 nucleases is stated.

statements.text: Across more than 10,000 cancer genomes, elevated N4BP2 expression predicted chromothripsis and copy number amplification.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Analysis of more than 10,000 human cancer genomes revealed elevated N4BP2 expression to be predictive of chromothripsis and copy number amplifications, including ecDNA.
statements.note: The genome count and both predicted features match.

statements.text: Pharmacological inhibition of N4BP2 reduces ecDNA formation in glioma cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: N4BP2 promoted genome rearrangements (including chromothripsis), formation of extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) in drug-induced gene amplification
statements.note: N4BP2 effects were established through an siRNA screen and genetic models; no inhibitor is mentioned.

statements.text: N4BP2 suppressed tumour cell proliferation in an induced model of human high-grade glioma.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: N4BP2 promoted genome rearrangements (including chromothripsis), formation of extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) in drug-induced gene amplification, tumorigenesis, and tumor cell proliferation in an induced model of human high-grade glioma.
statements.note: N4BP2 promoted, rather than suppressed, proliferation in the glioma model.

statements.text: Genome size in plant-parasitic nematodes scaled with total TE content across the 26 species.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: To investigate genome size variation and evolution in plant-parasitic nematodes, TE composition, diversity, and evolution were analysed in 26 plant-parasitic nematodes from 9 distinct genera in Clade IV.
statements.note: Genome size variation motivated the study, but no result linking genome size to TE content is reported.

statements.text: TE composition was analysed in 26 plant-parasitic nematode species from nine genera in Clade IV.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: TE composition, diversity, and evolution were analysed in 26 plant-parasitic nematodes from 9 distinct genera in Clade IV.
statements.note: The species and genus counts match the abstract.

statements.text: Species lacking certain DNA transposon or retrotransposon superfamilies showed correspondingly impoverished TE content.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: despite certain species lacking specific types of DNA transposons or retrotransposon superfamilies, they still exhibit a diverse range of TE content.
statements.note: The abstract stresses that such species still show diverse TE content.

statements.text: Gypsy superfamily elements in plant-parasitic nematodes encode aspartic proteases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the Gypsy superfamilies were found to encode Aspartic proteases in the plant-parasitic nematodes.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: The species and subspecies of the complex share closed, largely overlapping pan-genomes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The species and subspecies all display open and distinct pan-genomes
statements.note: The pan-genomes are described as open and distinct, not closed and overlapping.

statements.text: E. xiangfangensis isolates were more often carbapenem-resistant than E. hoffmannii isolates.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The E. hormaechei complex displays a highly mutable resistome, with most taxa being multidrug resistant.
statements.note: No antibiotic class and no between-species resistance comparison is given.

statements.text: Phylogenomics split E. hormaechei into three predicted species, with E. xiangfangensis further containing three putative subspecies.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: comprising three predicted species, E. hormaechei, E. hoffmannii and E. xiangfangensis, with the latter putatively comprising three distinct subspecies, namely oharae, steigerwaltii and xiangfangensis.
statements.note: Three species and three subspecies of E. xiangfangensis are listed.

statements.text: Most taxa within the E. hormaechei complex were multidrug resistant.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The E. hormaechei complex displays a highly mutable resistome, with most taxa being multidrug resistant.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: In the UW cohort, HRDetect-high patients had a median overall survival of 6.2 years versus 4.1 years for the others.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 6.2 vs. 4.1 years; hazard ratio (HR), 0.6; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.41-0.87; P = 0.007
statements.note: The median survival figures are given with HR 0.6.

statements.text: Rearrangement signature profiling identified 11 genomic clusters, with RS1, RS14 and RS18 profiles linked to better survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: RS profiling uncovered 11 genomic clusters, with specific RS profiles (RS1, RS14, and RS18) correlating with poor survival.
statements.note: Those RS profiles correlated with poor survival, not better survival.

statements.text: In ARIEL2, HRDetect-high tumours responded to rucaparib at a rate of 54% compared with 22.5% for other tumours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In ARIEL2, HRDetect-high tumors showed better PARPi responses, with improved progression-free survival (11.1 vs. 7.1 months; HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.26-0.74; P = 0.03) and response rates (54% vs. 22.5%).
statements.note: Response rates of 54% versus 22.5% are reported for ARIEL2.

statements.text: HRDetect-intermediate tumours had survival outcomes between those of the HRDetect-high and HRDetect-low groups.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: A substantial fraction (23.2%) fell into an HRDetect-intermediate category, highlighting greater genomic heterogeneity than currently appreciated.
statements.note: The intermediate group's size is reported but its survival is not.

statements.text: PIK3CA mutations in cfDNA were associated with shorter overall survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The main objective of this study was to estimate the frequency and clinical value of the ESR1 and PIK3CA mutations identified in circulating free DNA (cfDNA.)
statements.note: PIK3CA appears only in the objective; no PIK3CA result is reported.

statements.text: ESR1 mutation frequency in advanced luminal breast cancer depended on the type of treatment received.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: ESR1 mutations are more frequent in patients with advanced luminal breast cancer regardless of the type of the treatment.
statements.note: The abstract says the higher frequency held regardless of treatment type.

statements.text: Blood from 179 metastatic breast cancer patients was analysed for CTC counts and ESR1 and PIK3CA mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the CTC number and ESR1 and PIK3CA mutations in blood collected from 179 patients with metastatic breast cancer
statements.note: The cohort size and measured markers are stated.

statements.text: No ESR1 mutations were found in primary tumour samples, indicating they arise mainly during progression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ESR1 mutations appear primarily during progression, as no mutations were found in primary tumor samples.
statements.note: Both the absence in primaries and the inference are stated.

statements.text: GAPF-seq combined with machine learning separated 39 breast tumours from matched control DNA with an AUC of 0.955.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: GAPF-seq differentiated 39 breast tumors from matched control DNA with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.955.
statements.note: The tumour count and AUC match.

statements.text: GAPF-seq palindrome signals declined after androgen deprivation therapy in prostate cancer patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: As a simple and agnostic liquid biopsy approach, GAPF-seq could fill this technological gap, offering unique cancer-specific SV profiles.
statements.note: No treatment or longitudinal sampling is described.

statements.text: The cfDNA proof-of-concept study included 27 control individuals and 24 prostate cancer patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cfDNA from 27 prostate cancer patients and 24 control individuals yielded an average AUC of 0.896.
statements.note: The group sizes are swapped: 27 patients and 24 controls.

statements.text: High-coverage bins on the X chromosome were a nearly decisive feature in the cfDNA analysis and were tied to androgen receptor amplification.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: HCBs on the X chromosome emerged as a nearly decisive feature and were linked to androgen receptor gene amplification.
statements.note: Both the decisive role and the AR amplification link are stated.

statements.text: A positive MammaTrace result preceded clinical recurrence by a median of 45 days.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: preceded clinical or radiologic recurrence by a median of 457 days
statements.note: The median lead time was 457 days, roughly ten times longer.

statements.text: MammaTrace reached 91% sensitivity and 83% specificity over a median follow-up of 12.4 months.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: MammaTrace achieved a sensitivity of 91% and specificity of 83%, with a median follow-up of 12.4 months.
statements.note: All three figures match the abstract.

statements.text: MammaTrace sensitivity was higher in HER2-positive than in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: MammaTrace was evaluated in an independent longitudinal cohort of early-stage breast cancer patients treated with curative intent.
statements.note: No breakdown by breast cancer subtype is reported.

statements.text: MammaTrace is a plasma-only methylation assay built from DMRs identified in metastatic breast cancer by whole-genome bisulfite sequencing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a plasma-only cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation-based MRD assay, informed by differentially methylated regions (DMRs) identified in MBC using whole genome bisulfite sequencing.
statements.note: The assay design is described exactly this way in the methods.

statements.text: The HERV-K envelope protein was identified as an important driver of lymphoma cell growth.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with the HERV-K envelope protein identified as a crucial contributor to lymphoma cell growth.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: FF-01 is a humanized camelid nanobody that kills lymphoma cells through complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The newly developed nanobody FF-01 demonstrates anti-lymphoma activity through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and internalization.
statements.note: The mechanisms reported are antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and internalization, not complement-dependent cytotoxicity.

statements.text: FF-01 reduced tumour burden in a mouse xenograft model of DLBCL.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The newly developed nanobody FF-01 demonstrates anti-lymphoma activity through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and internalization.
statements.note: The listed methods are all in vitro or computational; no animal experiment is mentioned.

statements.text: DLBCL patients with high HERV-K113 expression showed activation of antiviral response pathways.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients with high HERV-K113 expression show activation of pathways related to antiviral responses, suggesting a viral mimicry state.
statements.note: Stated directly, with the viral mimicry interpretation.

statements.text: Of 22 women with advanced high-grade serous ovarian cancer, only four had complete records.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We selected 22 women diagnosed with advanced high-grade serous ovarian cancer, of which only 4 had complete records.
statements.note: Both numbers are stated in the methods.

statements.text: cfDNA and ctDNA levels showed no significant correlation with CA125.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cfDNA and ctDNA correlated significantly with CA125.
statements.note: The abstract reports a significant correlation.

statements.text: Serial cfDNA and ctDNA measurements signalled recurrence several months before CT imaging and CA125 changes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Following cfDNA and ctDNA over time indicated a recurrence several months earlier than computed tomography and CA125 changes.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: Patients with undetectable ctDNA after surgery had longer progression-free survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We aimed to demonstrate the usefulness of ctDNA and cell-free DNA (cfDNA) as a marker of complete cytoreduction and during follow-up in patients with advanced ovarian cancer.
statements.note: Survival outcomes are never reported.

statements.text: Radiomic features predicted EGFR mutation status more accurately than KRAS mutation status.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: when predicting the combined mutation status of gene pairs (e.g., EGFR and ROS1)
statements.note: No per-gene accuracies are given and KRAS is not mentioned.

statements.text: Radiomic features predicted single gene mutation status from liquid biopsy with classification accuracy of around 0.60.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a moderate association between radiomic features and single gene mutations detected through liquid biopsy in NSCLC patients, with classification accuracies reaching approximately 0.60.
statements.note: The approximately 0.60 accuracy for single genes is stated.

statements.text: Predicting the combined mutation status of gene pairs improved accuracy to about 0.90 compared with single genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the classification task involved three classes and yielded substantially lower accuracy (approximately 0.30)
statements.note: Gene-pair prediction dropped accuracy to about 0.30, not raised it.

statements.text: Second-order texture features carried the greatest importance in the models.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Notably, second-order texture features showed the highest importance in the models.
statements.note: Stated directly in the discussion.

statements.text: Patients with a clock-like COSMIC_5 signature survived longer than those with a UV signature.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients with UV signature had longer survival compared to patients with clock-like and COSMIC 30 ( p < 0.0001).
statements.note: The UV signature group survived longer; the clock-like signature predicted poor survival.

statements.text: Patients with the UV signature responded better to immune checkpoint inhibitors than those with the clock-like signature.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We aimed to assess whether genomic alterations may predict survival after the development of stage IV disease, irrespective of received therapy.
statements.note: Survival was analysed irrespective of therapy; no treatment-response data are given.

statements.text: The cohort's mutational profile matched the UV signature COSMIC_7 with a cosine similarity of 0.932.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: UV signature COSMIC_7 (cosine-similarity 0.932)
statements.note: The cosine similarity is given as 0.932.

statements.text: No single gene alteration or combination of alterations could be dichotomously linked to survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: no individual gene alterations, or combinations of alterations, could be dichotomously associated with survival.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: By pathological stage, KRAS G12C ctDNA was detected only in stage III patients, in 4 of 11.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In overall pathological staging, KRAS G12C ctDNA was detected exclusively in liquid biopsies of stage III patients (4/11, 36%).
statements.note: Exclusive detection in pathological stage III, 4 of 11, is stated.

statements.text: KRAS ctDNA positivity was linked to a median overall survival of 21 months versus 41 months for ctDNA-negative patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: KRAS ctDNA positivity was associated with shorter overall survival (median OS 21 months vs. 41 months
statements.note: The median OS figures match.

statements.text: KRAS G12V ctDNA-positive patients had worse survival than KRAS G12C ctDNA-positive patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: KRAS ctDNA positivity was associated with shorter overall survival (median OS 21 months vs. 41 months
statements.note: Survival is reported for KRAS ctDNA positivity overall, not by variant.

statements.text: KRAS G12C ctDNA positivity was associated with smaller tumour size and absence of nodal involvement.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: G12C ctDNA positivity was associated with larger tumour size, presence of nodal involvement, and higher overall pathological stage.
statements.note: The associations were with larger tumours and nodal involvement, the opposite.

statements.text: Radiation alone killed tumour organoids more effectively than combined chemoradiation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Chemoradiation led to greater tumor organoid killing compared to radiation or chemotherapy alone.
statements.note: Chemoradiation outperformed either modality alone.

statements.text: TransferNet-PDO separated tumour from normal organoids on digital histopathology images with an AUC of at least 0.88.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: which accurately distinguished tumor versus normal PDOs in culture using digital histopathology images (AUC≥0.88).
statements.note: The AUC threshold of 0.88 is stated.

statements.text: PDO establishment success was higher for oral cavity tumours than for laryngeal tumours.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we established PDOs from surgically resected fresh tissues of human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) across anatomical sites, tumor T-categories, and sample types.
statements.note: Multiple anatomical sites were included, but no site-specific success rates are reported.

statements.text: Cisplatin lowered organoid viability, while cetuximab and lenvatinib had little effect.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: cisplatin reduced cell viability, whereas cetuximab and lenvatinib had minimal effects.
statements.note: Stated directly in the drug sensitivity results.

statements.text: bta-miR-30a-5p is expressed at higher levels in the mammary gland of high-yield dairy cattle.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The mir-30 family is closely associated with biological processes influencing the quantity and quality of agricultural products.
statements.note: The comparison was in silico on reference genomes; no expression or tissue data are reported.

statements.text: The recombination products gave rise to 129 microRNAs in cattle and 51 in bison, of which 50 were shared.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: These recombination products served as sources of 51 microRNAs in bison and 129 microRNAs in cattle, including 50 microRNAs that were similar in both species.
statements.note: All three counts match the abstract.

statements.text: Nearly all cattle-only microRNAs from the trinomial recombination products belonged to the mir-30 family.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A total of 79 microRNAs were found only in cattle trinomial recombination products, with 98% belonging to the mir-30 family
statements.note: 98% of the 79 cattle-only microRNAs were mir-30 family members.

statements.text: The LINE/ERV/LINE recombination products were absent from the corresponding 12-gene block in bison.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: highly conserved recombination products (with more than 81.5% identity) were present in the corresponding block of 12 genes in bison.
statements.note: The products were present and highly conserved in bison.

statements.text: Of 145 first-round participants, 136 (96.8%) responded in the second round.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Of 145 participants in the first round, 136 (96.8%) responded in the second round.
statements.note: The participation figures match.

statements.text: The consensus recommended HIPEC alongside cytoreductive surgery for eligible patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: For both pathways, early referral to a peritoneal surface malignancy (PSM) center should be made for patients with CRC-PM.
statements.note: HIPEC is never mentioned in the abstract.

statements.text: For synchronous CRC-PM, the consensus prioritised upfront cytoreductive surgery over systemic therapy.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: For the synchronous pathway, upfront cytoreductive surgery was de-emphasized in favor of systemic therapy.
statements.note: Upfront surgery was de-emphasised in favour of systemic therapy.

statements.text: ctDNA testing received only a weak recommendation because evidence for detecting and monitoring peritoneal metastases is limited.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: including only a weak recommendation for circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) testing given limited evidence of its utility in detecting and monitoring PM.
statements.note: Both the weak recommendation and its reason are stated.

statements.text: TE transcript levels in PE placentas were inversely correlated with type I interferon pathway activity.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A higher TE transcript level correlates with the type I interferon (IFN I) pathway
statements.note: The correlation reported is positive: higher TE transcripts with IFN I pathway activity.

statements.text: The TE-transcript classifier predicted preeclampsia in the validation cohort with AUC 0.88, 81% sensitivity and 74% positive predictive value.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88, 81% sensitivity, and 74% positive predictive value (PPV).
statements.note: All three metrics match.

statements.text: Low-dose aspirin lowers placental TE transcript levels in women at risk of preeclampsia.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: maternal cfRNA TE signature accurately predicts early diagnosis of PE, which can improve prophylaxis and obstetric outcomes.
statements.note: Prophylaxis is mentioned as a potential benefit of prediction; no intervention was tested.

statements.text: Higher ERV and LINE1 expression in PE placentas was accompanied by higher histone acetylation at their regulatory elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Increased expression of endogenous retrovirus (ERV) and long interspersed nuclear element 1 (L1, LINE1) subfamilies of TEs is associated with higher histone acetylation levels at their regulatory elements.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: H101 injection increased tumour-infiltrating CD8+ T cells in post-treatment biopsies.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Somatic mutations, including high-frequency mutations, microsatellite instability (MSI) status, tumor mutation burden (TMB), clonal evolution, and mutational signature were analyzed.
statements.note: Only exome-derived genomic features were analysed; no immune profiling is reported.

statements.text: Nine complete and three partial responses among 17 patients gave an objective response rate of 70.6%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Complete response was achieved in 9 patients, 3 patients achieved partial response, and 2 patients had stable disease, resulting in an objective response rate (ORR) of 70.6% (95% CI: 46.4%-96.7%).
statements.note: The response counts and ORR match.

statements.text: Higher tumour mutation burden correlated with better response to H101.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients with lower TMB were correlated with improved H101 response rates ( P =0.044)
statements.note: Lower, not higher, TMB was associated with improved response.

statements.text: KMT2D and ADAP1 mutations were associated with worse progression-free and/or overall survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: KMT2D and ADAP1 mutations were associated with inferior progression-free survival (PFS) and/or overall survival (OS) ( P <0.05).
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: Edema crossing the midline had the highest selection frequency, 55.8%, among 31 reproducible MRI features.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Among 31 reproducible MRI-derived features, edema crossing the midline had the highest selection frequency (55.8%).
statements.note: Both the feature count and selection frequency match.

statements.text: Edema crossing the midline was associated with markedly higher odds of plasma ctDNA positivity.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: edema crossing the midline was linked to markedly lower odds of plasma ctDNA positivity (Firth-penalized OR 0.068).
statements.note: The odds were markedly lower (OR 0.068), not higher.

statements.text: The cohort comprised 25 patients with CNS-involving DLBCL who contributed 46 paired ctDNA-MRI evaluations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 25 patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the CNS (primary or secondary) contributed 46 paired plasma ctDNA and contrast-enhanced brain MRI evaluations.
statements.note: Patient and evaluation counts match.

statements.text: Edema crossing the midline reflects blood-brain barrier integrity that limits ctDNA release into plasma.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Reproducible MRI features, especially edema crossing the midline, were inversely associated with plasma ctDNA positivity across repeated evaluations.
statements.note: The abstract reports an association only and proposes no mechanism.

statements.text: BTA insertion sites were characterised by high DNA methylation and low H3K27ac, typical of heterochromatin.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: These insertion sites have typical euchromatin features, including low levels of DNA methylation and high levels of H3K27ac.
statements.note: The sites showed euchromatic features: low methylation and high H3K27ac.

statements.text: A transposon capture assay identified 79 new insertions of BTA and BTA-like elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A transposon capture assay revealed 79 novel insertions for BTA and BTA-like elements.
statements.note: The count of 79 novel insertions is stated.

statements.text: BTA transposition is triggered by heat stress during maize propagation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: an active transposition event was identified during the propagation of maize inbred line B73.
statements.note: The transposition event is reported but no trigger or condition is studied.

statements.text: The BTA insertion in ZmSWEET4c left transcript levels unchanged but lowered protein abundance.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The BTA insertion does not affect transcript abundance but reduces protein abundance of ZmSWEET4c
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: The BLOODPAC Consortium formed a brain tumour working group in 2022 to standardise preanalytical variables for CSF liquid biopsy.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the Blood Profiling Atlas in Cancer (BLOODPAC) Consortium launched a BT Working Group in 2022.
statements.note: The year and purpose are stated in the purpose section.

statements.text: The Working Group recommended processing CSF within two hours of collection.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The Working Group agreed on a recommended list of preanalytical minimum technical data elements, clinical context data elements, and patient context data elements
statements.note: Categories of variables are described, but no specific variable or threshold is named.

statements.text: A subset of critical-priority variables became required annotations for CSF liquid biopsy data submitted to the BLOODPAC Data Commons.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A subset of variables were considered to be of critical priority and are designated as required annotations to submissions of cfDNA-based CSF liquid biopsy sample data into the BLOODPAC Data Commons.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: The Working Group restricted its recommendations to patients with primary brain malignancies, excluding metastatic disease.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: key preanalytical variables for cfDNA-based CSF liquid biopsy in patients with primary and metastatic brain malignancies.
statements.note: The variables cover both primary and metastatic brain malignancies.

statements.text: Most patients with circulating ESR1 mutations carried a single variant rather than polyclonal mutations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Eleven patients had polyclonal ctESR1m within the ligand-binding domain, six at baseline, while five harboured a single ctESR1m variant.
statements.note: Eleven of the sixteen had polyclonal mutations; only five had a single variant.

statements.text: Twenty-one of 24 patients (88%) carried at least one somatic mutation in cfDNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Twenty one of the 24 patients (88%) had at least one somatic mutation in cfDNA (248 total mutations across 10 genes).
statements.note: The count and percentage match.

statements.text: ESR1 mutations were detected in the primary tumour DNA of the 16 patients with available tissue.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Thirteen of 16 tumour DNA samples harboured at least one somatic mutation across nine genes.
statements.note: Tumour DNA mutations are counted but the genes involved are not named, so ESR1 status in tissue is unknown.

statements.text: Circulating ESR1 mutations were found in patients with both stable and progressive disease, with no clear link to progression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: present in 16 patients (76%) with both stable (SD) and progressive disease (PD), showing no clear association with disease progression.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: Targeted sequencing of uterine aspirates found pathogenic variants in 95.45% of tumours and allowed ctDNA monitoring in 89.4% of patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: pathogenetic variants in the 95,45% of the tumours and ctDNA levels could be monitored in the 89,4% of the patients.
statements.note: Both percentages match (the abstract uses decimal commas).

statements.text: Baseline cfDNA and ctDNA levels lost prognostic significance once tumours were stratified by histopathological risk factors.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: this approach remains clinically significant when stratifying tumours based on histopathological risk factors
statements.note: The abstract says the prognostic value remained significant after stratification.

statements.text: Longitudinal cfDNA/ctDNA analysis flagged relapsing patients months before any clinical evidence appeared.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: longitudinal analyses of cfDNA/ctDNA proved to be a powerful asset to identify patients undergoing relapse, months prior to the arisen of any clinical evidence.
statements.note: Stated directly in the results.

statements.text: ctDNA detection at baseline was more frequent in serous than in endometrioid endometrial carcinomas.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: High levels of cfDNA and detectable levels of ctDNA at baseline correlated with poor prognosis, for both DFS (p-value<0.0001; HR=9,25) and DSS (p-value<0.0001; HR=11,20).
statements.note: No breakdown by histological subtype is reported.
